newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thousands of poor villagers protest in Bangkok.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of poor villagers protest in Bangkok.

text.p: Thousands of impoverished Thais who have been camped outside Government House for the past two months on Sunday staged a massive rally in Bangkok to drum up support for their cause.

The demonstrators, most of them villagers from the poor northeastern region of Thailand, waved brightly coloured flags and marched to the beat of drums as they walked about two km (1.2 miles) to the city's Royal Grounds from their makeshift homes outside Government House.

The peaceful group, organised by a movement called the Assembly of the Poor, wore hats or towels on their heads to protect themselves from the scorching mid-afternoon sun and carried banners demanding social justice and equality for all people of Thailand.

"Don't forget the poor are also people of this country," Dang Noisang, one of the organisers of the protest, said through a loudspeaker. "These people are the people who feed the country. They are farmers, fishermen and labourers."
"What we are calling for is to be recognised as a part of the country," he said as he travelled in a truck ahead of the marchers. "We may not pay a lot of taxes but we are a part of the country."
Organisers expected between 10,000 to 20,000 demonstrators to assemble at the Royal Grounds to join in on a rally to mobilise public support for their cause.

Nitirat Sapsomboon, spokesman for the Assembly of the Poor, was quoted by the Bangkok Post newspaper as saying impoverished people were determined to stay on in Bangkok until all their problems were solved.
When the thousands of protesters arrived in Bangkok in January they demanded the government free them from their long-standing debts to the state-owned Bank of Agriculture and Cooperatives.
They also called on the government to settle land disputes, offer compensation for building dams on land they claim and pay higher prices for their agricultural produce.
They have had several rounds of talks with government officials, including with Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, but have not resolved all their problems.
